title: Dexcom G6, XDrip and Tandem t:slim X2
body:
Hello, I started to use the t:slim X2 pump with a Dexcom G6 two weeks ago.
I can simultaneously see sugar values at the pump, the mobile and the watch (Sony SmartWatch 3) if the mobile works as collector. The Dexcom G6 must be bi-channel so both the mobile and the pump can connect at the same time.
However, if I set the watch as collector, the pump keeps reading the G6, but XDrip doesn't give any reading. I would prefer to use the watch as collector, so I don't have to take the phone with me all the time or take out the pump from my pocket to have a look at the sugar readings.
Any idea of what could be happening?
Thanks a lot.

comments.body:
Did you enable "Only use Wear" in the Android Wear Integration settings?
As far as I know, you also have to enable "Force Wear Collection Service".

Yes, I have been using the watch as collector for a couple of years before having the pump, so I know the settings needed. But with those settings, with is basically "Force Wear Collection Service", the watch doesn't work as collector while the pump is connected to the G6 Transmitter. If I set the mobile as collector the mobile works, and If I switch off  the pump and set the watch as collector the watch connects.

@Gonzmdv This is fascinating!
I know that G6 has two slots.
I know that  xDrip (phone) and the Dexcom app use the mobile slot; the Dexcom receiver and the t:slim pump use the other slot.

That's why you cannot use xDrip and the Dexcom app at the same time to collect from the same transmitter.
And, you cannot use the Dexcom receiver and the t:slim pump at the same time to collect from the same transmitter.

What you are describing, I had never heard before.  It may suggest that your watch also requires the second (receiver) slot.

By any chance, have you had any other observations you can share?

I have the same problem except the configuration I have is SSW3, Samsung phone, Dexcom g6 and, Dexcom receiver. The Dexcom receiver is not working since I started the SSW3. I wish I could collect the readings on Dexcom receiver as it would be the simplest way for my my endo to have it.

I am thinking about getting the tslim pump so your question caught my eye.  Unfortunately, the only way way to run all three components is the enable watch as a collector option is disabled. The only reason I got the SSW3 is to allow it to run as a standalone collector, so it is a pain.

@ubersputnik So, you don't have a t:slim pump.
How could you be having the same problem then?

It looks like the Sony Smart Watch 3, the t:slim X2 pump and the Dexcom receiver runs through the same G6 transmitter channel, while the mobile runs through the other. I have read somewhere that the new Dexcom G7 transmitter will be multichannel, so maybe we will have all of them working as collectors at the same time in a few months. Let's cross fingers.

No, the SSW3 uses the phone slot. The t:slim X2 is using the medical device slot. Hence, you cannot connect the Dexcom receiver and the t:slim X2 at the same time (see also [Can I use a separate Dexcom receiver to view my data, in addition to the pump?](https://support.tandemdiabetes.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038805554)) but you should be able to use SSW3 as collector side-by-side to the t:slim X2.

BTW: The G6 is multi-channel (two channels), already. Don't expect too much from the G7.

As I said when I opened this thread, I have never been able to have the pump and the watch working as collector at the same time, so they must be using the same slot. If the watch is connected and working as collector the pump doesn't connect, and the opposite, if the pump is connected, the watch will not connect as collector.
